abstract: P2CS-Web (https://www.p2cs.org) links genome-wide two-component system (TCS) repertoires to protein domain architectures, genomic neighbourhoods, and sequence-identity clusters. The current release covers 392 075 bacterial genomes and 25 663 653 TCS-associated genes, including 12 517 906 encoding histidine kinases (HKs) and 12 774 395 encoding response regulators (RRs). HK and RR protein sequences are grouped into 2 931 715 and 2 479 169 sequence clusters, respectively, each represented by a single sequence. Genome, gene, and cluster pages combine these annotations with member taxonomy and local gene organization. An additional annotation layer applies 18 HisKA-like profile HMMs to HK candidates whose primary annotation lacks a HisKA domain. The resulting matches can be inspected against the original classification and domain coordinates. Genome and cluster comparisons, representative-sequence alignments, configurable exports, and a versioned API allow users to examine TCS diversity and download sequences and associated annotations for subsequent analyses.
